title: Noise kernel phase identity
statement: Let $N\in\mathbb N$, $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and $a,b\colon\{1,\ldots,N\}\to\mathbb R$. With $\sigma(\mathrm{false})=1$, $\sigma(\mathrm{true})=-1$, and $K_\rho(x,y)=\prod_{i=1}^N\frac{1+\rho\sigma(x_i)\sigma(y_i)}2$, one has $2^{-N}\sum_{x,y\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}^N}K_\rho(x,y)\exp\!\bigl(i\sum_{i=1}^N(a_i\sigma(x_i)+b_i\sigma(y_i))\bigr)=\prod_{i=1}^N\left(\frac{1+\rho}{2}\cos(a_i+b_i)+\frac{1-\rho}{2}\cos(a_i-b_i)\right)$.
hypotheses_covered: $a,b$ are real-valued functions on the $N$ coordinates
